review_evidence: This 1,771-file HOL unit is entirely under examples/ and spans machine-code models, logic, algebra, formal languages, computability, lambda calculus, crypto, separation logic, theorem-prover examples and many other object-level formal developments.

Directory naming alone was not used to filter `examples`, `dev`, `tests` or demo scripts; the unit is retained because these files contain actual theory scripts, definitions and theorem statements valuable as prior art.
summary: Reviewed the large HOL examples unit and retained all 1,771 primary files; it is formal example/theory content rather than distribution tooling.

review_evidence: Ran a HOL-declaration-marker grep (Theory/Theorem/Definition/Datatype/store_thm/prove\(/new_theory/Define) over all 4 files: keccakScript.sml 242 matches, balanced_mapScript.sml 206 matches, SlaneyRLScript.sml 16 matches, l3_equivalenceLib.sml 0 matches (flagged for closer inspection since the marker set targets Theory-file syntax).

Read the first 40 lines of examples/Crypto/Keccak/keccakScript.sml (143474 bytes): a `Theory keccak` block citing the SHA-3/FIPS-202 standard, with proved Theorems (e.g. LENGTH_PAD_RIGHT_0_8_word_to_bin_list) using real HOL tactics (rw, Cases_on, irule, gs) and QED-closed proofs. Genuine formal cryptography content.

Read the first 40 lines of examples/data-structures/balanced_bst/balanced_mapScript.sml (133394 bytes): a `Theory balanced_map` block with proved Theorems (list_rel_lem1, list_rel_lem2) about LIST_REL and list truncation, each closed with QED via genuine tactic proofs (Induct_on, qexists_tac, rw, fs). Genuine formal data-structure verification content.

Read the first 40 lines of examples/logic/relevant-logic/SlaneyRLScript.sml (12917 bytes): a `Theory SlaneyRL` block defining a `Datatype: s_prop` (the relevant-logic proposition syntax), a `Definition s_DIMP_def`, custom infix notation via set_fixity/overload_on, and the start of an `Inductive slaney_provable` block (the provability relation). This is the canonical relevant-logic formalization cross-referenced by developers/bench-metis-order.sml (reviewed separately under unit RRU-ce77fb5c5a7c), confirming it is genuine object-logic content.

Read the first 80 lines plus grepped the whole of examples/l3-machine-code/arm8/asl-equiv/l3_equivalenceLib.sml (16445 bytes, 432 lines): a `structure l3_equivalenceLib` that opens 9+ HOL theories (armv86aTheory, arm8Theory, arm8_stepTheory, wordsTheory, bitstringTheory, etc.) and l3_equivalence_lemmasTheory/l3_equivalenceTheory, and defines custom proof tactics (l3_eval, l3_eval_tac, mk_blast_thm using blastLib.BBLAST_CONV/BBLAST_PROVE, qcollapse_tac, l3_decode) that manipulate real HOL terms and internally prove/rewrite theorems as part of an ARM8-to-ASL semantic-equivalence proof development. The 0-match grep result reflects that this is a `*Lib.sml` proof-support module (tactics/term manipulation) rather than a `*Script.sml` theorem-statement file, but its content is genuine formal-verification infrastructure built directly on real theories, not build/distribution tooling; it fails FILTER-004's exclusion test.

All 4 files sit within the examples/ subtree the prior review retained wholesale; independent re-assessment of each file's actual content, per FILTER-022, confirms the same disposition for these specific files.
